name: Going am Wilden Kaiser
kurzbeschreibung: Village with a direct view of the Wilder Kaiser and access to the ski world – perfect for nature lovers.
beschreibung:
Overview

Going am Wilden Kaiser is situated at an elevation of 772 metres in the Tyrolean district of Kitzbühel, nestled directly at the foot of the rugged limestone crags of the Kaiser Mountains. The picturesque village is home to approximately 1,950 residents, occupying a charming landscape between St. Johann in Tirol and Ellmau that stretches from the gentle valley floor up to the 2,242-metre Goinger Halt summit. Despite its international renown as a principal filming location for the popular television series Der Bergdoktor, Going has carefully preserved its tranquil alpine village character. The historic village square delights visitors with its heritage fountain, traditional wooden chalets, and the ornate Rococo parish church framed dramatically by the towering cliffs of the Wilder Kaiser. Going represents an idyllic haven for families, hikers, and relaxation seekers.

History

Settlement around Going dates back to pre-Roman times; Celtic miners were extracting copper and silver at nearby Rehrobichl as early as 800 BC. The community was first documented between 1140 and 1145 as Gouingen in the traditions of Baumburg Abbey, a Bavarian name meaning the settlement of the clan of Guowo. During the 16th century, mining flourished again under the Kitzbühel trade guilds, with the local Heilig-Geist shaft descending to a depth of over 880 metres, ranking among the deepest mine shafts in the world at the time. The architectural jewel of the village is the Parish Church of the Holy Cross, constructed between 1774 and 1775 by master builder Andreas Hueber. Widely praised as one of the finest Rococo churches in Tyrol, it boasts expressive ceiling frescoes by Matthias Kirchner, ornate stucco work, and a Late Gothic Madonna from 1480. In the village square stands the heritage St. Florian fountain, and during summer months, the renowned Going Craft Market revives centuries of rural craftsmanship.

Getting There

By car, travellers from Germany can reach Going toll-free and without an Austrian motorway vignette by exiting the A12 motorway at Kufstein-Süd and taking federal roads B173 and B178 past Söll and Ellmau directly to Going. From Salzburg, the road approaches via Lofer and St. Johann in Tirol. Rail passengers arrive at nearby stations in St. Johann in Tirol, Kitzbühel, or Wörgl Hauptbahnhof, all served by express trains. From the stations, scheduled VVT bus route 4060 provides regular connections to Going. Throughout the summer, the complimentary KaiserJet shuttle bus operates between Going, Ellmau, Scheffau, and Söll, stopping directly at the swimming lake and cable car base stations.

Tips

A prime summer attraction is the Badesee Going, repeatedly voted the most beautiful natural swimming lake in Tyrol, fed directly by pure springs from the Kaiser massif and featuring expansive sunbathing lawns, a children's white sand beach, and a 100-metre outdoor water slide. The Astbergbahn chairlift whisks visitors up to the 1,267-metre Astberg summit to enjoy the mirror-like Astbergsee lake and comfortable wooden panoramic loungers at the Kaiser Cinema. In winter, Going provides the eastern entry point into the SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser-Brixental, offering over 270 kilometres of interconnected ski slopes. Fans of television culture can stroll around the historic village square featuring the exterior of the Gasthof Wilder Kaiser, while mountaineers challenge the ascent of Goinger Halt or the world-famous climbing routes around the Schleier Waterfall.
metaDescription: Going am Wilden Kaiser: Picturesque village at the foot of the Wilder Kaiser, Badesee swimming lake, Rococo church, and SkiWelt access.
